generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

The order's woody program (growth plan G2.3a), on the broadleaf base: Asteraceae's own program grows its herbs, so its trees and shrubs take the order's, which gives the values its species leave unset, as the broadleaf program's defaults until then.

traits.inflorescence_unit.note: VicFlora's family description: the flowers sit packed on a shared receptacle in heads (capitula), each almost always ringed by an involucre of bracts.

traits.leaf_arrangement.note: VicFlora's family description: leaves one or two to a node, rarely more; it names neither as the usual state.

traits.leaf_division.note: Abrams and Ferris (vol. 4, 1960, p. 98), Compositae: leaves entire or more or less dissected, that is one blade however deeply cut. Watson and Dallwitz (1992) give simple or compound; the compound leaves of a few genera (Bidens, Dahlia and some Coreopsis) make compound the rare state (inferred: neither source gives a share).

traits.division_pattern.note: Watson and Dallwitz (1992), Compositae: dissected blades pinnatifid, palmatifid, runcinate or spinose, with no frequencies. Pinnatifid and runcinate cuts run along a midrib, so pinnate is the usual state; palmatifid blades are the few (inferred).

traits.fruit_type.note: VicFlora's family description: the fruit is usually a cypsela (a one-seeded fruit from an inferior ovary), often topped by a pappus.

rules.note: How PlantGen draws the daisy family's heads, a choice of the model's (spec rework P2): a head is laid out from its florets (`crate::capitula`), its phyllaries in rows round its foot, its receptacle domed as its shape says, its disc florets packed in a sunflower spiral and opening from the rim inward, rays round a radiate head, straps filling a ligulate one; an array of heads is a cluster of such heads (spec rework L1). Its size is its involucre's, as floras measure it, plus a ray on either side. The heights the shape words give the receptacle and the pappus lengths of crowns, scales and awns are the model's. A leaf's card is as wide, for its length, as the flora's blades; a head's size, and the share of its cluster it takes, follow from its involucre and rays.

appearance.organs.flower.colour.why: A head's rays (or straps) are drawn in the look's colour and its disc in the accent: a radiate head's rays in the rays' stated colour, a discoid head's florets in theirs, a head of straps in the straps'; where the kind's own colour is not stated, the flower's. The disc takes the disc florets' colour.

appearance.organs.*.shape.kind.why: A head is drawn as its kind: rays round a disc, a disc alone, or straps alone. A disciform head's threadlike outer florets barely show, so it is drawn as a discoid one.

appearance.organs.*.shape.rays.why: A radiate head draws each of its ray florets as a ray; the other kinds have none.

appearance.organs.*.shape.disc.why: A radiate head's disc is about as wide as its involucre, with a ray's length beyond it on either side: the disc's share of the head's width. A head of disc florets alone is its disc, its florets spreading a little past the involucre's rim. A head of straps opens to about twice its involucre's width, the model's choice from photographs of cat's ears and hawkweeds, so its involucre is half of it.

appearance.organs.*.shape.florets.why: A head draws each of its disc florets, or of a head of straps each strap, on its receptacle, up to the 1,000 a head can hold.

appearance.organs.*.shape.phyllaries.why: A head draws each of its phyllaries round its involucre, up to 200.

appearance.organs.*.shape.series.why: The phyllaries stand in their rows, the outer ones shorter.

appearance.organs.*.shape.involucre.why: The involucre is as tall for its width as the flora measures it.

appearance.organs.*.shape.receptacle.why: The receptacle's dome is as tall for its radius as its shape word says: none for flat, a third for convex, the radius for a half sphere, twice it for a cone; between two words, between their heights.

appearance.organs.*.shape.pappus.why: A fruit in seed carries its pappus: bristles as long as the flora measures them for the disc's radius, which is about the involucre's; a crown, scales and awns, which floras seldom measure, a tenth, a quarter and a half of it.

generator.params.flower_size.why: A herb's lone head is as wide as its involucre, as floras measure it, with a ray beyond it on either side; a head of disc florets alone spreads a little past its involucre (the disc's share of the head, 0.85), and an open head of straps to twice it. Where a herb's flower is a cluster of heads, its species sets the cluster's length by hand and the cluster's size its heads.

generator.params.bloom_size.why: A shrub's lone head is as wide as a herb's: its involucre and a ray either side, or its disc a little past its involucre, or its straps twice it.

appearance.organs.*.inflorescence.size.why: A cluster of heads draws each head as wide as a lone head is, its involucre and a ray either side, as a share of the cluster's length.

appearance.organs.leaf.shape.width.why: A blade is as wide for its length as its flora measures it, the middle of each range; it takes the place of the width the kingdom's rule gives the blade's shape word.

appearance.organs.basal.shape.width.why: A blade is as wide for its length as its flora measures it, the middle of each range; it takes the place of the width the kingdom's rule gives the blade's shape word.
